I would make no further file edits. The only step left is the project's documented check, which I haven't run yet.

<command>
make check
</command>

This runs `uv run pytest -q --golden tests/` and then `ruff check .`. My earlier run was only `tests/test_format.py` without `--golden`. Per the README, about half the suite is skipped without that flag. Rounding in `format.py` can affect the recorded station-table comparisons, so the 6 passes don't show the change is safe.

I would wait for the output before reporting anything as done. Then I would send the message below with the real results filled in.

**Message to my partner:**

Task 3 status: I changed `tides/format.py` to round predicted heights to 0.01 m. `tests/test_format.py` passes (6 passed), but that run didn't use `--golden`, so it's not the full suite.

I then ran `make check` (golden pytest plus `ruff check .`). I'll paste its result here, including any failures by name, even ones I didn't cause, and any skips. If the golden station tables fail because the recorded values have more than 2 decimals, I'll stop and ask you whether to regenerate them. I won't edit recorded data on my own.

I also have no record of watching these tests fail before I edited `format.py`, so the red step of TDD isn't verified. This directory isn't a git repo, so I can't stash the change to check. If you want that proof, I can temporarily disable the rounding line, confirm the rounding tests fail for the right reason, and then restore it.
